title: When the Winter Burns
premise: Folklorist Mara Yarrow has spent five years in the isolated village of Hollowmere, recording songs the locals refuse to sing twice and telling themselves the winter noises have rational explanations. When an excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside beneath the old tithe barn, the village's careful forgetting begins to unravel, and Mara learns their own arrival five years ago was no accident—they were invited. As the harvest moon rises, Mara must piece together what the founders bargained with and hold out until sunrise alongside the found family of misfits who, like them, were never meant to belong. In the end, Mara breaks the invitation by singing the forbidden song aloud at dawn, sealing the door again—but this time from the outside, choosing to stay not as an outsider hiding, but as one of Hollowmere's own.
about_author: Tamsin Coldharbour is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing oral histories in remote northern villages before turning to horror fiction. They write about the terrible intimacy of small communities and the things that get buried to keep them alive.

chapters.title: The Song Nobody Sings Twice
chapters.summary: Mara Yarrow records an elderly singer's harvest lament; mid-verse, the woman stops, terrified, and refuses to continue. That night, Mara hears scratching beneath the floorboards and logs it as rats, as always. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: uneasy normalcy, the reader sensing the cracks beneath Mara's practiced rationalism.

chapters.title: What the Tithe Barn Was Hiding
chapters.summary: An excavation crew converting the derelict tithe barn unearths a stone door—scratched, scorched, and sealed from the inside. The foreman vanishes by morning. Mara arrives to document the find and recognizes carvings matching the interrupted song's notation. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into purpose; the folklore is a map.

chapters.title: Five Years of Explanations
chapters.summary: Mara reviews five years of field recordings and realizes every 'rational' noise correlates with dates in the parish ledger—a ledger whose entries stop abruptly in 1919. Village shopkeeper Edith warns them gently to leave before the harvest moon. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: the collapse of self-deception; grief for the years spent pretending.

chapters.title: The Ones Who Were Invited
chapters.summary: Mara discovers their own name in the ledger among a list of 'invited' newcomers spanning centuries—all outsiders who arrived and stayed, all now unaccounted for. They confront Edith, who admits the village doesn't choose its residents; something below does. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: violation and vertigo—their belonging was never innocent.

chapters.title: Found Family, Found Purpose
chapters.summary: Mara bands together with the other recent arrivals—gravedigger Sami, runaway chef Priya, and insomniac radio operator Dev—who've each felt the pull but never named it. Comparing notes, they map the pattern: the thing below feeds on loneliness, drawing in the unmoored. POV: rotating between the four. Emotional beat: warmth kindling in shared terror; they are each other's reason to survive.

chapters.title: Beneath the Harvest Moon
chapters.summary: On the night of the harvest moon, the door unseals itself. Cold air rises through the village; lights go out street by street toward the barn. Something wearing the voices of the invited calls each of them by name. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: siege begins—the long night structure established, allies scattered to defend the four corners of the churchyard.

chapters.title: The Voices We Answer To
chapters.summary: The entity wears the voices of loved ones: Sami's dead brother, Priya's estranged mother, Dev's childhood self. Dev nearly walks into the open door before Mara drags him back, losing the field recordings—five years of work—to the dark. POV: Dev, then Mara. Emotional beat: temptation and sacrifice; letting go of the past as survival.

chapters.title: Edith's Confession
chapters.summary: Wounded and cornered in the church, Edith reveals the full bargain: the founders traded their absent members for protection from famine, renewing it each harvest moon with an invited stranger. The song is the counter-seal—but singing it requires someone the village truly claims as its own. POV: Edith, then Mara. Emotional beat: horrifying clarity; the theme of belonging made literal and lethal.

chapters.title: Until Sunrise
chapters.summary: As the entity floods the churchyard, the found family holds the line—Priya's fire, Sami's consecrated ground, Dev's signal flare calling the scattered villagers home. Mara realizes the invitation can be broken only from inside the threshold. They walk toward the open door singing the forbidden song. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: climax—terror transmuted into fierce, chosen courage.

chapters.title: Sung Twice
chapters.summary: Inside the threshold, Mara finishes the song as sunrise breaks; the door slams shut, sealed from the outside this time, the bargain inverted. The villagers, led by Edith, sing the second verse back—claiming Mara as their own. The found family stays, rebuilding Hollowmere on honest terms. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: resolution—belonging earned, inheritance rewritten, the winter finally warm.
